issues.claim: T-V3-39's timing cell (V03 l. 2906) lands "(e) and (h)'s exports from P5", and (h) re-reads "drawing and exports" across the lifecycle. V03 §8's P4 tests cell (l. 2943, edited this round) runs "T-V3-39 but (e), its scrub across the run at the later of P4 and V06's E6", so P4's exit includes (h)'s exports before P5's exporters. P5's tests cell (l. 2944) runs only "T-V3-39 (e)". The milestone cells omit a split the test's own timing cell names.
issues.required_change: V03 §8's P4 tests cell: "T-V3-39 but (e), its scrub across the run at the later of P4 and V06's E6;" → "T-V3-39 but (e) and (h)'s exports, its scrub across the run at the later of P4 and V06's E6;". P5's tests cell: "T-V3-39 (e)" → "T-V3-39 (e) and (h)'s exports".

issues.claim: T-V4-63 (V04 l. 3146, written this round from R5-02's V04 end) ends "the frame growth's case keeping every old station and its vaults". §2.7's support step (7) (base l. 2623–2628) keeps every old station and "every span between two of them". It runs (1)–(5) and the span rule from the old deck's last interior station to the new end, or with none from the other foot, so the old end span is re-derived. V04 §3.10 (l. 2284–2286) then lays "a new `vault` span's vault" and deletes "one whose span is gone". Where the old end span (or a one-span deck's only span) was `vault`, a correct build removes that vault or re-lays it under a new key, and "its vaults" read as every vault of the old deck fails it. The mechanism is (7)'s and §3.10's, so nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: T-V4-63: "the frame growth's case keeping every old station and its vaults" → "the frame growth's case keeping every old station and, with the same id and footprint, the arch vault of every old span between two of them (§2.7's support step (7)), the span from the old deck's last interior station (with none, its one span) re-derived with the extension and its vault laid or deleted by its new span (V04 §3.10)".

issues.claim: One fix with VAL-R5-04, at a site it does not list. R5-04's one comparison (§6.3 *Plan damage*, base l. 10006–10008) compares an element "only from its entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (a)–(b); …)". T-V4-82 (b) (V04 l. 3165) restates it without the entry week: "each element damaged exactly while the level is above 0 and at least its threshold (§6.3 *Plan damage*'s comparison)". R5-01 (2) (c) puts the tests in the sweep. Its fixtures hold no element entering the plan after the level rose, so nothing tested changes.
issues.required_change: T-V4-82 (b): "each element damaged exactly while the level is above 0 and at least its threshold (§6.3 *Plan damage*'s comparison)" → "each element damaged exactly while the level is above 0 and at least its threshold, compared from its entry week into the plan (§6.3 *Plan damage*'s one comparison; V03 §5.6 (2) (a)–(b))".

issues.claim: One fix with VRC5T-03, at a site it does not list. T-V3-39 runs "on the damage fixtures", which hold the struck district (V03 §7, l. 2848–2853). Under the look a building's panel lists the look's damage at its drawn level under `info.crisis.ruinedFor` (V03 §4.5, l. 2321–2322). The `plan` section's rows read the own level and carry no look (V03 §4.6, l. 2386–2387; T-V3-40 (d)). So T-V3-39 (f) (l. 2906) — "the panel's damage lines and the `plan` section's rows read the same `PlanDamage` — one line or row per kind present, none on a never-decayed building" — fails a correct build on a never-decayed house of that district in the condition's weeks. VRC5T-03's V03 end names (g) only. T-V3-40 (e) runs the look's lines, so nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: T-V3-39 (f): "(f) the panel's damage lines and the `plan` section's rows read the same `PlanDamage` — one line or row per kind present, none on a never-decayed building —" → "(f) on a building no disaster look stands over (the look's lines are T-V3-40 (e)'s), the panel's damage lines and the `plan` section's rows read the same `PlanDamage` — one line or row per kind present, none on a never-decayed building —".
